worker-fleet Workflow v3 • Claude Code + OpenCode + ChatGPT/Codex

Multi-Harness Orchestration. Fleet Control Live.

Instead of juggling multiple disjointed terminals across different AI tools, orchestrate everything through a unified Router agent or monitor your fleet in real time via the Fleet Control Dashboard (:3080). Dispatches self-contained feature tickets across Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex CLI into isolated Git worktrees, tracks token telemetry on disk, and lets you approve and unblock tickets directly from your mobile phone.

Multi-Model Flexibility

Multi-Harness Architecture & The /setup Skill

Different tasks demand different model balances. worker-fleet v3 lets you run on Claude Code, OpenCode, or hybrid delegation with OpenAI Codex CLI with 4 battle-tested presets or your own custom role mapping.

Preset Name Target Harness router (Orchestrator) worker & teammate reproducer & reviewer watchdog, tester, merger
hybrid-bridge Recommended Claude Code + Codex Claude opus (High) Claude sonnet (High) Claude sonnet + codex exec review Claude sonnet (Medium)
claude-default Claude Code Claude opus (High) Claude sonnet (High) Claude sonnet (High) Claude sonnet (Medium)
deepseek-lean Claude Code / OpenCode sonnet / deepseek-chat sonnet / deepseek-reasoner sonnet / deepseek-reasoner haiku / deepseek-chat
opencode-openai OpenCode (opencode) OpenAI gpt-5 (High) OpenAI gpt-5 (Medium) OpenAI o3 (High) OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini

⚡ One-Shot or Interactive /setup

Run /setup with no flags to interview you one question at a time (Harness → Preset → Concurrency → Dashboard), or pass key-value flags in one shot: 

/setup harness=both preset=hybrid-bridge max_workers=4 dashboard=on tunnel=cloudflared

🔄 Deterministic OpenCode Sync

Running .claude/scripts/apply-setup.py automatically generates opencode.json (with {file:.opencode/agents/...} prompt bindings) and all 9 subagent files inside .opencode/agents/*.md.

🌉 Codex CLI Delegation Bridge

When hybrid review is enabled, worker and reviewer agents call .claude/scripts/delegate-task.sh codex review to automatically capture your git diff for a second-opinion pass via OpenAI Codex CLI.

Component Roster

The 2 Skills & 8 Specialized Agents

Each agent has a strict single responsibility and tailored model settings so you don't burn Opus tokens on routine implementation or background monitoring.

/setup Skill
Configures CLI harness, model presets, concurrency, dev ports, and Fleet Control Dashboard. Updates specs/worker-fleet.config.json and runs apply-setup.py.
Path: .claude/skills/setup/SKILL.md
/write-tickets Skill
Reads your codebase and interviews you one question at a time until zero ambiguity remains. Generates numbered ticket folders (rd.md + eval.md) and updates specs/tickets/BOARD.md.
Path: .claude/skills/write-tickets/SKILL.md
router Opus / GPT-5 • Orchestrator
Your single chat interface. Starts watchdog and Fleet Control at Step 0, dispatches ready tickets from BOARD.md, checks results.md, and forwards mobile user-decision.md unblocks.
Port: N/A (Never edits application code)
watchdog Sonnet / Mini • 150k Compact
Runs in the background every 10 minutes via watchdog-check.sh. Alerts @main if a worker goes silent (>15m), loops on an error, edits a ## Do not touch file, or receives a mobile decision.
Setting: autoCompactWindow: 150000
worker Sonnet • Worktree
Builds one solo ticket inside an isolated Git worktree. Updates job/status.json, runs tester and reviewer (with optional Codex CLI bridge), writes results.md + evidence/, and commits.
Ports: :3101, :3102, :3103... (Accounts t001+)
teammate Sonnet • Agent Team
Used for foundational or multi-surface team tickets. Teammates first negotiate and lock shared schemas/APIs in contract.md before building their assigned areas in parallel.
Requires: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1
tester & reviewer Sonnet • QA Pair
Spawned by each worker before committing. tester executes every check in eval.md via agent-browser and saves screenshots to evidence/; reviewer audits git diff against rd.md.
Read-Only Verification Subagents
merger & checker Sonnet • Integration
merger lands verified branches onto main, runs lint/build, and marks BOARD.md as done. checker then smoke-tests main on port :3000 like a first-time user.
Main Checkout • Port :3000 (Account t000)
reproducer Sonnet / o3 • Hotfix :3090
Triggered on live bug reports or checker failures. Reproduces the bug twice in an isolated worktree on :3090, auto-fixes localized bugs (1–3 files) on its own branch, or files a root-cause report.
Worktree Isolation • Port :3090 (Account t090)
Real-Time Observability

Fleet Control Dashboard (:3080) & Mobile Tunnel

Monitor your parallel worktrees, review visual browser evidence, inspect multi-harness token telemetry, and approve tickets from your phone without opening a terminal.

📊 1. Live Kanban & Worktree Matrix

Polls /api/state every 3s. Shows tickets in draft, ready, in-progress, blocked, and done. Real-time worker cards display assigned port, TCP connection health, phase, and heartbeat stall warnings (>15m).

📷 2. Visual Evidence Gallery

Clicking any ticket opens a slide-over drawer with 5 tabs: Requirements (rd.md + user-decision.md), Evaluation (eval.md), Contract (contract.md), Results & Git Commits (results.md), and a full-screen screenshot lightbox.

💎 3. Multi-Harness Token Telemetry

Zero external API keys required! Directly parses session logs from disk: Claude Code (~/.claude/projects/), OpenCode SQLite (opencode.db), and Codex rollout files (~/.codex/sessions/). Calculates total cost, role consumption, and prompt cache savings.

📱 4. PIN-Protected Mobile Unblocking

Accessed via Cloudflare Quick Tunnel or ngrok. Allows you to flip tickets from draft → ready or answer questions for blocked workers by writing user-decision.md and transitioning their status from your phone.

⚡

How to Launch Fleet Control & Mobile Tunnel

Run the dashboard launcher script in your terminal. It boots the Python server on :3080, connects the tunnel, and prints an interactive ASCII QR code:

bash — Start Dashboard & Tunnel 
bash .claude/scripts/start-dashboard.sh

Scan the terminal QR code with your mobile camera to open https://xxxx.trycloudflare.com/?token=... instantly.

Step-by-Step Guide

How to Install & Run the Workflow (v3)

Follow these 5 steps to configure your environment, generate tickets, and start autonomous parallel builds.

1

Install into Your Repo & Install Prerequisites

Run the installer from a worker-fleet checkout against your existing repository (it copies the workflow files, backs up anything it would overwrite, and creates the specs/ skeleton), then install Vercel's agent-browser CLI for automated UI verification:

bash — Terminal in project root 
bash .claude/scripts/install.sh /path/to/your-repo
npm install -g agent-browser
2

Configure Your Environment with /setup

Launch your CLI and run /setup to pick your CLI harness and model preset:

Claude Code / OpenCode Prompt 
/setup harness=both preset=hybrid-bridge max_workers=4 dashboard=on tunnel=cloudflared

This writes specs/worker-fleet.config.json, updates .claude/agents/*.md, generates opencode.json + .opencode/agents/*.md, and creates the dashboard auth token.

3

Generate Tickets Using /write-tickets

Describe your features in plain English or reference your PRD file:

Claude Code / OpenCode Prompt 
/write-tickets Write tickets for all features in specs/PRD.md

Answer the skill's clarifying questions one at a time. It populates specs/tickets/NNN-slug/rd.md, eval.md, and updates specs/tickets/BOARD.md with status draft.

4

Launch Fleet Control Dashboard & Approve Tickets

Start Fleet Control in the background:

bash — Terminal in project root 
bash .claude/scripts/start-dashboard.sh

Open http://127.0.0.1:3080 (or scan the mobile QR code) and click Approve & Mark Ready on tickets you want to dispatch, or tell your AI assistant:

CLI Prompt 
Mark tickets 001, 002, and 003 as ready in specs/tickets/BOARD.md
5

Launch the Autonomous router Session

Start your chosen CLI harness as the router orchestrator:

Option A: Claude Code CLI 
claude --agent router --name router --permission-mode auto
Option B: OpenCode CLI 
opencode --agent router

Inside the router chat, kick off the autonomous build:

Router Prompt 
Start building all ready tickets on the board.
Project Lifecycle & Evolution

How the Workflow Evolves Over Time

Real software isn't built in a single batch. Below is the complete lifecycle showing how BOARD.md, your Git branches, the agents, and Fleet Control evolve from Day 1 foundation to parallel sprints, mid-flight hotfixes, and future feature requests.

Figure 2: Evolutionary timeline of a repository managed by worker-fleet v3 across days, sprints, and remote mobile sessions.
Stage 1 • T+00:00 (Foundation Sprint)
Team Ticket Builds the Core & Unlocks Dependent Solo Tickets
You start with Ticket 001 marked ready (Mode: team) while Tickets 002 and 003 are marked ready with waits for 001.

1. Router launches watchdog and starts the Fleet Control server on :3080.
2. The teammates negotiate and lock specs/tickets/001-auth-schema/contract.md so their API routes and TypeScript interfaces match.
3. Teammates build their assigned surfaces, run tester (via agent-browser), and report to the router.
4. Merger lands 001 into main and marks it done on BOARD.md.
Stage 2 • T+00:45 (Parallel Solo Sprint)
Router Auto-Dispatches Independent Tickets Simultaneously
Because 001 is now done, the router scans BOARD.md, sees that 002 and 003 now have all dependencies satisfied, and launches them in parallel:

• Worker A gets 002 on port :3101 (Account t001).
• Worker B gets 003 on port :3102 (Account t002).
• Both workers write heartbeats to job/status.json visible immediately on the Fleet Control matrix.
Stage 3 • Mid-Flight Bug Report & Reproducer Autofix
Handling Bugs Without Stopping Running Workers
If you or checker discover a broken user flow, prompt the router without killing your parallel workers:
Prompt to Running Router 
The login form throws a 500 when submitting an email with a '+' sign. Investigate and fix.
1. Router spawns reproducer in an isolated worktree on port :3090.
2. Reproducer verifies the bug twice in agent-browser.
3. Since the fix is local (≤3 files), reproducer commits on a branch and hands off to merger.
4. Workers building 002 and 003 continue uninterrupted!
Stage 4 • Adding New Feature Requests Over Time
Incremental Ticket Numbering Without Resetting the Board
When you want to add new features days or weeks later, run /write-tickets again. It automatically finds the highest existing ticket number (e.g., 003), creates 004-... and 005-..., preserves all done rows in specs/tickets/BOARD.md, and adds ## Do not touch rules so new workers never collide with existing modules.
Stage 5 • Self-Healing & Mobile Unblocking
How Watchdog & Fleet Control Handle Stalls or Blockers
• Stalled Worker Recovery: Every 10 minutes, watchdog executes watchdog-check.sh. If a worker's heartbeat exceeds 15 minutes, watchdog messages @main to inspect or reboot the worker.
• Remote Unblocking via Phone: If a worker hits a product ambiguity, it updates status to blocked. Fleet Control notifies your phone via Cloudflare Tunnel, where you can type your decision (writing user-decision.md) and unblock the agent immediately.
